title: Controlled kNN by Hidden-Dimension Factorial at 500 Universes and Top100 Halos
scientific_question: How do periodic-kNN connectivity and hidden dimension jointly affect Omega_m prediction within the canonical EvolveGCN-H and Static GCN protocols?

fields_allowed_to_differ.reason: The analysis intentionally compares the complete canonical EvolveGCN-H and Static GCN protocols.
EvolveGCN-H uses temporal graph sequences; Static GCN uses final-snapshot static graphs.
The established model-specific protocols use batch sizes 4 and 8.
The established protocols use two EvolveGCN-H layers and three Static GCN layers.
Mean temporal pooling applies only to EvolveGCN-H.
Each architecture retains its established regression head.
EvolveGCN-H uses five snapshots while Static GCN uses the final snapshot.
The dataset representation is temporal for EvolveGCN-H and final-snapshot static for Static GCN.
Five temporal snapshots apply only to EvolveGCN-H.
Final-snapshot selection metadata applies only to Static GCN.

controlled_variables_summary: Within each model, k, hidden dimension, and seed are the only varying experimental factors. All rows use the same 500-universe population, Top100 raw-mass selection, seven node features, minmax normalization, periodic kNN construction, and exact seed-specific split IDs.
limitations_summary: Only three seeds are available. Cross-model differences are descriptive comparisons of complete protocols and do not isolate a causal effect of temporal processing.
comparison_statement: Controlled within each model for k and hidden dimension. Static-versus-Evolve results are descriptive protocol-level comparisons because temporal input, architecture, layer count, batch size, and regression heads intentionally differ.
